we developed a new gene delivery system with SPIO nanocrystal core and Stearic-LPEI shell via self-assembly, which can effectively bind with and protect the mcDNA from enzymatic degradation, and can noninvasively monitor the gene delivery via MRI.
the self-assembled Stearic-LPWI-SPIO nanoparticles are highly effective for mcDNA delivery and ultrasensitive for MRI of mcDNA transfection.
a self-assembled SPIO nanoparticle was prepared for the highly sensitive MRI of gene delivery and the SPIO nanoparticle can effectively deliver mcDNA and protect the mcDNA from enzymatic degradation.

the design of novel gene delivery systems with high transfection efficiency and ultrasensitive in vivo imaging ability, which will provide a new strategy for the development of gene therapy and diagnosis.
the design, synthesis and characterization of a novel self-assembled SPIO-based gene delivery system.
the design and fabrication of SPIO nanoparticles for the non-invasive monitoring of gene delivery, which may have a great potential in gene therapy.

the Stearic-Lwpei-SPIO nanoparticle is a promising platform for highly sensitive MRI monitoring of gene delivery and has great potential for gene therapeutic applications.
the self-assembled Stearic-LWPEN-SPIO nanosystem is highly sensitive to the transfection of mc-DNA, and the transfection can be monitored in real time with MRI.
the self-assembled magnetic theranoostic nanoparticles have great potentials in highly sensitive MRI of mcDNA delivery and gene therapy.

the Stearic-LwPEI-SPIO/mcDNA nanoparticle is a promising theranostic system for non-invasive MRI monitoring of gene delivery.
a novel gene delivery system was successfully developed with SPIO as the core and biocompatible Stearic-LWPENI as the shell.
the self-assembled Stearic-LWPEN-SPIO nanoparticles can be used as a theranostic platform for highly sensitive MRI and efficient mcDNA delivery.

SPIO nanoparticles are promising for highly sensitive MRI detection of gene delivery.
